factual_claims.claim: The global market for AI hiring technology was growing rapidly prior to 2022.
LLMs are pretrained on unlabeled text corpora containing tens of billions of books.
New York City's Local Law 144, effective July 2023, mandates bias audits for AI hiring tools.
Only 19 audits linked to NYC Local Law 144 were published in the first 6 months after it took effect.
The study analyzed 801 applicants for K-12 teaching positions in a large American public school district.
The applicant pool for the study was 67% women, 2% Asian, 45% Black, 10% Hispanic, and 38% White.
The study audited 11 different LLMs from OpenAI, Mistral, and Anthropic.
LLMs showed moderate race and gender disparities, with a slight preference for women and non-White candidates in hiring ratings.
The study found that LLMs could correctly identify the intended race and gender of synthetic applicants over 90% of the time.

The challenge of auditing AI systems for bias is a central concern across all three POV camps, though they differ in their interpretation of the necessity, efficacy, and accountability implications of such audits.
unmapped_concepts.Accelerationist Interpretation: Auditing is a pragmatic, iterative tool for improving AI performance and reliability, accelerating the path to robust, beneficial systems.
unmapped_concepts.Safetyist Interpretation: Auditing is a critical, necessary safety requirement to identify and mitigate harmful biases before they cause catastrophic, irreversible societal damage.
unmapped_concepts.Skeptic Interpretation: Auditing is a fundamental requirement for accountability, exposing the present harms and biases of AI systems that powerful developers would otherwise obscure.
